In practice budget_exhausted is appended INSIDE the `if exit_code != 0` branch, so engineer_exit_nonzero is always present with it, and a killed engineer never writes its SESSION_CLOSE so relay_not_closed is present too. Both real budget-exhausted movements recorded exactly ['engineer_exit_nonzero', 'budget_exhausted', 'relay_not_closed'].

risks: Implementing the allowlist as an exclusion list, so a future unknown reason silently becomes resumable. R-2b and AC-3 exist for this.
Dropping the requirement that budget_exhausted be present, which would make any nonzero exit with an open relay resumable.
Deleting the superseded test instead of updating it, losing the coverage that found this defect.
Widening the entailed set because a third reason seems harmless.
Letting verify state leak into the predicate after GOV.ORCH.10-A section 3 decided it must not.

in: Replace the predicate in _is_resumable_budget_failure with GOV.ORCH.10-A R-2a: the record is resumable when budget_exhausted is present in its recorded failure_reasons and every other reason present belongs to a closed entailed set. That set is exactly {engineer_exit_nonzero, relay_not_closed} and nothing else.

Define the entailed set as a named module-level constant with a comment naming GOV.ORCH.10-A R-2a and the reason each member is entailed, so a future reader sees why membership is closed rather than guessing.

R-2b, default-closed: any reason NOT in the entailed set blocks the resume, including a reason that does not exist today. Implement this as membership in the allowlist, never as exclusion of a list of known-bad reasons.
R-2c: budget_exhausted must still be PRESENT. A record carrying only engineer_exit_nonzero, or only relay_not_closed, or both without budget_exhausted, is not a budget failure and stays terminal.
Keep everything else in _is_resumable_budget_failure unchanged, including its phase == PHASE_FAILED guard and its role as the single place both decide_start and _do_start read the decision from.

Update the tests written against the superseded R-2 rather than deleting them. GOV.ORCH.10 section 4 item 2's mixed-reason test becomes GOV.ORCH.10-A acceptance item 3: keep the test, change its reason set to one containing a reason OUTSIDE the entailed table, and keep asserting dispatch.

Add tests for GOV.ORCH.10-A acceptance items 1, 2, 3 and 4. Item 1 must use the exact set ['engineer_exit_nonzero', 'budget_exhausted', 'relay_not_closed'], because that is what both real movements produced. Item 3 must use an INVENTED reason name that does not exist in the codebase, so the test proves the allowlist rather than a list of today's reasons.
out: Changing how failure_reasons is constructed anywhere in the file. The reasons are an input to this decision, not something to reshape for it.

Making verify a recorded failure reason, or letting verify state influence the resume decision. GOV.ORCH.10-A section 3 decides this explicitly: a failed verify does NOT block a budget resume, because a run killed mid-work almost always has a red verify, and the safety is that verify runs again and the Product Owner assistant reviews the diff before any merge.
Changing the phase decision, TERMINAL_PHASES, retry_limit, DEFAULT_MAX_BUDGET_USD, or the R-3 ceiling refusal.

Widening the entailed set beyond the two reasons GOV.ORCH.10-A R-2a names. If a third reason looks like it belongs, that is an amendment to the contract and a RELAY_QUESTION here, not an implementation decision.
Any change outside scripts/orchestrator.py and tests/test_orchestrator.py.
Touching the state records of NXS-LOCAL-0130, 0131 or 0132.
